Access to PHI by a workforce member without a treatment, payment, or operations relationship is by definition unauthorized access and triggers the breach-response/risk-assessment workflow, so C3 is selected. C1 fails because an incidental disclosure is an unavoidable byproduct of a permitted use, whereas this was direct, purposeful record entry; C2 fails because the stem explicitly negates any care role, and education is not a blanket operations exception for identifiable records of patients outside one's assignment. For actions, A4 and A2 mirror and formalize the two steps the stem says RN Jordan has already begun — stopping access and initiating facility reporting — providing immediate containment plus the written incident report with access details and mitigation. A1 is contraindicated because it substitutes the involved employee's self-report for mandated reporting. A3 is contraindicated because incident reports are confidential quality/risk documents and are never referenced in the medical record. For parameters, P4 evaluates the immediate integrity of the response (Privacy Officer engaged, breach determination started, audit trail preserved as evidence), and P2 evaluates the downstream corrective outcome (targeted education and strengthened safeguards).
